sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮

translations.literal: Tiegezhu
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮，高昌人。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu was a man of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu was a native of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 世居五城，後徙京師。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in Wucheng, and later moved to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had lived for generations in Wucheng before relocating to the capital.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父達釋，有謀略，為國人所信服。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dashi was resourceful in counsel and trusted by the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dashi was a man of strategic talent whom his countrymen trusted.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，高昌國主懼，以錦衣、白貂帽召達釋與謀。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned west, the king of Gaochang was afraid and summoned Dashi to counsel, presenting brocade robes and a white sable cap.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taizu's western campaign the king of Gaochang grew fearful and called Dashi to council, honoring him with brocade garments and a white sable cap.

sentences.zh: 達釋知天命有歸，勸其主執贄稱臣，以安其國，由是號為尚書。

translations.literal: Dashi knew that Heaven's mandate had found its object and urged his lord to present tribute and declare himself a subject, thereby securing the state; for this he was styled Shangshu.
translations.idiomatic: Dashi saw that the mandate of Heaven had turned and urged his sovereign to submit with tribute and acknowledge vassalage, so as to preserve the kingdom; he was thereafter styled Shangshu.

sentences.zh: 太祖班師，諸王言於帝曰：「達釋之子野里朮驍勇善戰，所將部落又強大。

translations.literal: When the Taizu withdrew his army, the princes said to the emperor: "Dashi's son Yelizhu is fierce and brave in battle, and the tribes he leads are moreover powerful.
translations.idiomatic: As the Taizu led his forces home, the princes told the emperor, "Dashi's son Yelizhu is a daring and skilled fighter, and the tribes under his command are strong besides.

sentences.zh: 聞其人每思率衆效順而未有機便，盍致之乎？」

translations.literal: It is heard that this man constantly wishes to lead his followers in submission but has lacked the opportunity — why not summon him?"
translations.idiomatic: We hear he has long wished to bring his people over in loyalty but has never found the right moment — ought we not bring him in?"

sentences.zh: 太祖是其議，即詔給驛馬五百，迎與俱來。

translations.literal: The Taizu approved this plan and at once issued an edict granting five hundred relay horses to welcome him and bring him together with his household.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu agreed, and immediately ordered five hundred relay horses sent to escort him and his household to court.

sentences.zh: 既至，引見，甚器重之。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was presented in audience and greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived and was presented at court, the emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 丙午，太祖西征，野里朮別從親王按只台與敵戰有功，甚見親遇。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year, during the Taizu's western campaign, Yelizhu separately followed Prince Anzhitai and fought the enemy with merit, and was treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: In bingwu, on the Taizu's western campaign, Yelizhu served under Prince Anzhitai in a separate column, distinguished himself against the enemy, and won exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 王方以絳蓋障日而坐，及聞野里朮議事，喜見顏色，稱善久之，既退，撒其蓋送之十里。

translations.literal: The prince was just then seated with a crimson canopy shading the sun; when he heard Yelizhu's counsel he showed pleasure in his countenance and praised him at length, and when Yelizhu withdrew he removed the canopy and escorted him ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had been sitting beneath a crimson canopy to keep off the sun; when he heard Yelizhu speak on affairs of state his face brightened and he praised him at length, and when Yelizhu took his leave he set aside the canopy and saw him off for ten li.

sentences.zh: 遂得兼長四環衛之必闍赤。

translations.literal: He was then able concurrently to head the bichigchi of the four guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereafter appointed to head concurrently the bichigchi of all four guard corps.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從國兵討金，以戰功最多，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: In the renchen year he followed the national army in punishing Jin and, having the greatest battle merit, received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen he marched with the imperial forces against Jin, topped the rolls for battlefield merit, and was rewarded with exceptional largesse.

sentences.zh: 甲午，副忽都虎籍漢戶口，籌其賦役，分諸功臣以地，人服其敏。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year he assisted Huduhu in registering Han households, planning their taxes and corvée, and allotting land to meritorious ministers; people admired his efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu he assisted Huduhu in registering Han households, assessing taxes and labor obligations, and parceling out land among the meritorious — all marveled at his dispatch.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮，野里朮長子也，尤沉鷙有才。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu was the eldest son of Yelizhu and was especially deep, reserved, and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu, Yelizhu's eldest son, was notably deliberate, reserved, and gifted.

sentences.zh: 嘗有擁兵叛者，鐵哥朮率族人與戰于魚兒濼。

translations.literal: Once there was a rebel who gathered troops; Tiegezhu led his clansmen to fight him at Yuer Po.
translations.idiomatic: When a local chieftain raised troops in rebellion, Tiegezhu led his kinsmen against him at Yuer Po.

sentences.zh: 時軍興，簿檄繁急，鐵哥朮一以其國書識之，無遺失者，帝甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: At a time when the army was on campaign and registers and dispatches came in thick and fast, Tiegezhu kept track of them all in his own script without a single loss, and the emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: With the armies in the field and paperwork pouring in, Tiegezhu filed every document in his own script without losing a single item, to the emperor's high praise.

sentences.zh: 至元中，擢為棣州達魯花赤，遷德安府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan reign he was promoted to darughachi of Dizhou and then transferred to darughachi of De'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era he was raised to darughachi of Dizhou and later moved to the same post at De'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 適土人蔡知府者以衆叛，鐵哥朮率衆先登，冒矢石，身被數槍，猶戰不已，遂討平之。

translations.literal: It happened that a local man, Prefect Cai, rebelled with a crowd; Tiegezhu led his troops to scale the walls first, braved arrows and stones, took several spear wounds, and still fought on without cease until the rebellion was crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a local official, Prefect Cai, rose in rebellion with a mob; Tiegezhu led the assault over the walls, stood in the hail of missiles, took several spear wounds, and fought on until the rising was put down.

sentences.zh: 主將怒，將屠其城。

translations.literal: The commanding general was angry and was about to slaughter the city.
translations.idiomatic: The commander in chief, enraged, prepared to put the entire city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮請曰：「叛者蔡知府數人而已，城中之人何預焉。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu petitioned, saying: "The rebels are only Prefect Cai and a few others — what have the people in the city to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu pleaded: "The rebels are only Prefect Cai and a handful of his followers — the townspeople had no part in it.

sentences.zh: 盍誅其黨與而止，毋令濫及非辜。」

translations.literal: Why not execute their faction and stop there, and not let punishment spread indiscriminately to the innocent?"
translations.idiomatic: Execute the ringleaders and their accomplices and go no further — do not let punishment fall on the innocent."

sentences.zh: 主將嘉其誠懇，城遂得全。

translations.literal: The commander praised his earnestness, and the city was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: The commander admired his sincerity, and the city was spared.

sentences.zh: 累官至嘉議大夫、婺州路達魯花赤，所在咸著政蹟。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Grand Master of Palace Counsellor and darughachi of the Wuzhou Route; everywhere he served he left notable records of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Grand Master of Palace Counsellor and darughachi of the Wuzhou Route, earning a reputation for effective administration wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 大德己亥卒，成宗敕其孫海壽載其柩歸葬京師，贈榮祿大夫、江浙行省平章政事、柱國，封雲國公，諡簡肅。

translations.literal: He died in the jihai year of Dade; the Chengzong ordered his grandson Haishou to convey his coffin back for burial in the capital, and posthumously granted him Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, Pillar of the State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Yunguo, and gave him the posthumous title Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in jihai of the Dade era; the Chengzong commanded his grandson Haishou to bring his coffin home for burial in the capital and posthumously honored him as Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffing him as Duke of Yunguo with the posthumous name Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 子四人：義堅亞禮，幼給事裕宗宮。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Yijianyali, who from youth served in the palace of Prince Yuzong.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons. Yijianyali had served in Prince Yuzong's household from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，為中書省宣使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he became an emissary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 15 he was made an emissary of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗使河南，適汴、鄭大疫，義堅亞禮命所在村郭搆室廬，備醫藥，以畜病者，由是軍民全活者衆。

translations.literal: Once on a mission to Henan, it happened that Bian and Zheng suffered a great pestilence; Yijianyali ordered every village and hamlet along the way to erect lodges, stock medicines, and shelter the sick, whereby many soldiers and civilians were wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Henan he found Bian and Zheng in the grip of a severe epidemic; he ordered villages along his route to erect shelters, stock medicines, and take in the sick, saving a great many soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 遷直省舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant of the Direct Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the Direct Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 承中書檄徵考上都儲偫，及還，帝賜錦衣貂裘一襲，以旌其能。

translations.literal: He received a Central Secretariat dispatch to inspect and audit the reserves at Shangdu, and on his return the emperor bestowed one set of brocade robes and a sable fur coat to honor his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying a Central Secretariat commission to audit the stores at Shangdu, he returned to court and was rewarded with brocade robes and a sable fur coat in recognition of his competence.

sentences.zh: 出為湖州路達魯花赤，卒于官。

translations.literal: He went out as darughachi of the Huzhou Route and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as darughachi of the Huzhou Route and died in office.

sentences.zh: 月連朮，同知安陸府事。

translations.literal: Yuelianzhu was vice administrator of Anlu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelianzhu served as vice administrator of Anlu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八扎，同知宣政院事。

translations.literal: Bazha was vice administrator of the Xuanzheng Court.
translations.idiomatic: Bazha served as vice administrator of the Xuanzheng Court.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，海壽，義堅亞禮子也。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; Haishou was the son of Yijianyali.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine grandsons; Haishou was Yijianyali's son.

sentences.zh: 由宿衛世祖朝累官至太中大夫、杭州路達魯花赤，招復流民有恩惠。

translations.literal: From palace guard service in the Shizu's court he rose through offices to Grand Master of the Palace and darughachi of the Hangzhou Route, and in recalling displaced people showed kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an imperial guardsman under the Shizu, he rose to Grand Master of the Palace and darughachi of the Hangzhou Route, where he won gratitude for bringing back refugees.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈翰林直學士，封范陽郡侯，諡惠敏。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made a direct academician of the Hanlin Academy, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made a direct academician of the Hanlin Academy, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang, and given the posthumous name Huimin.

sentences.zh: 十年，改僉淮西等處行樞密院事，城正陽以扼淮海諸州兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to commissioner of the Huai-Xi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and walled Zhengyang to choke off the armies of the Huai-Hai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was reassigned as commissioner of the Huai-Xi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and built up Zhengyang to block the armies of the Huai and Hai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋陳奕率安豐、廬、壽等州兵數撓其役，塔出選精銳日十數戰，奕遁去，卒城正陽。

translations.literal: The Song general Chen Yi led the troops of Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures and repeatedly harassed the work; Tachu chose crack troops and fought ten or more battles a day; Yi fled, and at last Zhengyang was walled.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander Chen Yi led forces from Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures and repeatedly disrupted the works; Tachu picked elite troops and fought as many as a dozen engagements a day until Yi withdrew and Zhengyang was finally completed.

sentences.zh: 宋人復造戰艦於六安，欲攻正陽，塔出詢知之，率騎兵焚其艦。

translations.literal: The Song again built warships at Lu'an intending to attack Zhengyang; Tachu learned of it through inquiry and led cavalry to burn the ships.
translations.idiomatic: The Song rebuilt warships at Lu'an to strike Zhengyang; Tachu learned of the plan and led cavalry to burn the fleet.

sentences.zh: 餽饟久不繼，出兵據險，潛取安豐麥以餉軍，宋兵壁橫河口，塔出將奇兵大破之。

translations.literal: Provisions had long failed to arrive; he sent troops to hold difficult ground and secretly took Anfeng wheat to feed the army; Song troops encamped at Henghekou, and Tachu led a surprise force and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies long cut off, he seized strong positions, secretly harvested Anfeng grain to feed his men, and when Song forces camped at Henghekou he led a flanking column and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，朝議：「淮上諸郡，宋之北藩，城堅兵精，攻之不可猝下，徒老我師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the court deliberated: "The prefectures along the Huai are Song's northern bulwark — their walls are strong and their troops skilled; they cannot be taken in a rush, and we would only weary our armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the court debated the strategy: "The Huai prefectures are Song's northern rampart — their walls are strong and their garrisons seasoned; a headlong assault would only exhaust our forces.

sentences.zh: 宜先渡江翦其根本，留兵淮甸絕其救援，則長江可乘虛而渡也。」

translations.literal: It is fitting first to cross the Yangzi and cut their root, leaving troops in the Huai region to cut off relief — then the Great River may be crossed at its weak point."
translations.idiomatic: We should cross the Yangzi first and strike at their heartland, leaving troops in the Huai basin to sever reinforcements; then the great river can be crossed where it lies open."

sentences.zh: 於是以塔出為鎮國上將軍、淮西行省參知政事，帥師攻安豐、廬、壽等州，俘生口萬餘來獻，賜蒲萄酒二壺，仍以曹州官園為第宅，給城南閑田為牧地。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tachu was made General for the Pacification of the State and vice administrator of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat, and led troops to attack Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures; he presented more than ten thousand captives, was granted two jars of grape wine, and was given the official garden of Caozhou as his residence and idle fields south of the city as pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Tachu was accordingly made General for the Pacification of the State and vice administrator of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat, and led the assault on Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures; he sent more than ten thousand captives to court and received two jars of grape wine, the official garden at Caozhou as his residence, and idle fields south of the city for pasture.

sentences.zh: 宋夏貴帥舟師十萬圍正陽，決淮水灌城，幾陷，帝遣塔出往救之。

translations.literal: The Song commander Xia Gui led a fleet of one hundred thousand to besiege Zhengyang, breached the Huai to flood the city, and it nearly fell; the emperor sent Tachu to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song admiral Xia Gui brought a fleet of one hundred thousand to besiege Zhengyang, broke the Huai dikes to flood the city, and nearly took it; the emperor dispatched Tachu to the relief.

sentences.zh: 道出潁州，遇宋兵攻潁，戍卒僅數百人，盛暑，塔出即發公庫弓矢，驅市人出戰，預度潁之北關攻易破，乃急徙民入城伏兵以待。

translations.literal: On the road he passed through Yingzhou and met Song troops attacking Ying; the garrison was only a few hundred men; in the height of summer Tachu at once issued bows and arrows from the public storehouses, drove townspeople out to fight, judged that Ying's north gate would be easy to break, and urgently moved the people into the city and set ambushes to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Marching through Yingzhou he found Song forces assaulting the city; the garrison numbered only a few hundred. In the midsummer heat Tachu issued arms from the public stores, pressed townspeople into the fight, judged the north gate the weak point, hurried the populace inside, and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宋人果焚北關，火光屬天，塔出率衆從暗中射之，矢下如雨，宋軍退走至沙河，大破之，溺死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: That night the Song indeed burned the north gate; flames joined sky to sky; Tachu led his men to shoot from the darkness; arrows fell like rain; the Song army retreated to the Sha River and was utterly broken; those drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Song burned the north gate as he had foreseen, flames lighting the sky; Tachu rained arrows from the darkness, drove the enemy back to the Sha River, and broke them utterly — the drowned were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 明日，長驅直走正陽，時方霖雨，突圍入城，遂堅壁不出。

translations.literal: The next day he drove straight on to Zhengyang; it was then raining heavily; he broke through the encirclement into the city and then held the walls and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pressed on to Zhengyang through pouring rain, broke through the siege lines into the city, and shut the gates behind him.

sentences.zh: 俄復開霽，與右丞阿塔海分帥銳師以出，渡淮至中流，皆殊死戰，宋軍大潰，追數十里，斬首數千級，奪戰艦五百餘艘，遂解正陽之圍。

translations.literal: Soon the sky cleared again; he and the right councillor Atahai each led crack troops out, crossed the Huai to midstream, and all fought to the death; the Song army collapsed in great rout; they pursued for several tens of li, beheaded several thousand, seized more than five hundred warships, and thus lifted the siege of Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the weather cleared he and Right Councillor Atahai led elite troops out, crossed the Huai to midstream, and fought with desperate valor; the Song army broke and fled; they pursued for miles, took several thousand heads, captured more than five hundred warships, and raised the siege of Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 塔出乃上奏：「方事之殷，宜明賞罰，俾將士有所懲勸。」

translations.literal: Tachu then memorialized: "While affairs are pressing, rewards and punishments should be made clear so that officers and soldiers may have something to fear and to strive for."
translations.idiomatic: Tachu then memorialized: "With battle still raging, rewards and punishments should be made explicit so that officers and men know what to fear and what to strive for."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，頒賞有差。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and issued rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and distributed rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，淮西行省復為行院。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat was again made a branch bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat was reconstituted as a branch bureau.

sentences.zh: 塔出引兵渡淮，屯廬、揚間。

translations.literal: Tachu led troops across the Huai and encamped between Lu and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Tachu crossed the Huai with his army and encamped between Lu and Yang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從丞相伯顏以舟師與宋軍戰，宋軍大潰，其臣賈似道奔揚州，遂分兵四出，克池州，取太平，順流東下，至建康、丹徒、江陰、常州，皆望風迎降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the chief councillor Bayan with the fleet to fight the Song army; the Song army collapsed in great rout; their minister Jia Sidao fled to Yangzhou; they then divided troops in four directions, took Chizhou, seized Taiping, and went downstream east to Jiankang, Dantu, Jiangyin, and Changzhou — all submitted at the sight of their banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he followed Chief Councillor Bayan's fleet against the Song; the Song forces broke and fled; their minister Jia Sidao ran to Yangzhou; the armies fanned out in four columns, took Chizhou and Taiping, and swept downstream to Jiankang, Dantu, Jiangyin, and Changzhou, each city surrendering at the first approach.

sentences.zh: 時揚州未附，諜告揚州人將夜襲丹徒，守將乞援，塔出設伏以待，揚州軍果夜至，塔出扼西津邀擊之，殺獲溺死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Yangzhou had not yet submitted; spies reported that men of Yangzhou would raid Dantu by night; the defending general begged aid; Tachu set an ambush to wait; the Yangzhou army indeed came by night; Tachu held Xijin and intercepted them; those killed, captured, and drowned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had not yet submitted; intelligence warned of a night attack on Dantu; the garrison commander pleaded for help; Tachu laid an ambush; the Yangzhou force came as predicted; he held Xijin ford and struck them; the killed, captured, and drowned were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝賜玉帶旌其功，授淮東左副都元帥，仍佩金虎符。

translations.literal: On entering court the emperor bestowed a jade belt to honor his merit and appointed him left vice commander-in-chief of Huai-East, still bearing the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor awarded him a jade belt in recognition of his service and appointed him left vice commander-in-chief of Huai-East, retaining the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加通奉大夫、參知政事，領淮西行中書省事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and made vice administrator of government affairs, heading the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and vice administrator of government affairs, with charge of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時沿淮諸州新附，塔出禁侵掠，撫瘡痍，練士卒，備姦宄，境內帖然。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures along the Huai had newly submitted; Tachu forbade plunder, soothed the wounded land, drilled soldiers, and guarded against treachery; within the borders all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai prefectures had only just submitted; Tachu forbade looting, tended the war-ravaged countryside, drilled his troops, and guarded against subversion until the region lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 俄遷江西都元帥，征廣東，塔出宣布恩信，所至溪峒納款，廣東遂平。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander-in-chief of Jiangxi and campaigned in Guangdong; Tachu proclaimed grace and trust; wherever he went mountain valleys submitted; Guangdong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander-in-chief of Jiangxi and sent to conquer Guangdong; Tachu proclaimed clemency and good faith, and wherever he marched the hill peoples submitted until Guangdong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加賜雙虎符，為江西宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was further granted the double tiger tally and made Jiangxi pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received the double tiger tally and was appointed pacification commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宋益王昰、廣王昺走保嶺海，復改江西宣慰司為行中書省，遷治贛州，授塔出資政大夫、中書右丞，行中書省事。

translations.literal: The Song princes Yi and Bing fled to hold the Lingnan coast; the Jiangxi Pacification Commission was again changed to a Branch Secretariat, its seat moved to Ganzhou, and Tachu was made Grand Master for Governance, right councillor of the Central Secretariat, and charged with Branch Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Song princes Yi and Bing took refuge on the southern coast; the Jiangxi Pacification Commission was converted back to a Branch Secretariat with its seat at Ganzhou; Tachu was made Grand Master for Governance, right councillor of the Central Secretariat, and head of the branch administration.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以二王事入議。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he entered court to deliberate on the affair of the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he came to court to discuss the campaign against the two Song princes.

sentences.zh: 帝命張弘範、李恒緫兵進討，塔出留後，以供軍費。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng to command troops in advance against them; Tachu remained behind to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng to lead the expedition; Tachu stayed behind to provision the army.

sentences.zh: 初江西甫定，帝命隳其城，塔出即表言：「豫章諸郡皆瀕江為城，霖潦泛溢，無城必至墊溺，隳之不便。」

translations.literal: When Jiangxi had just been pacified the emperor ordered its walls demolished; Tachu at once memorialized: "The prefectures of Yuzhang all build their cities along the river; when heavy rains flood, without walls there will surely be inundation and drowning — to demolish them is not expedient."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi had only just been pacified when the emperor ordered its walls torn down; Tachu memorialized at once: "The Yuzhang prefectures all stand on the river; in seasons of flood the cities would be drowned without their walls — demolition is unwise."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 降附之初，有謀畔者，既敗獲矣，塔出謂同僚曰：「撫治乖方之所致也，中間豈無詿誤。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of submission there were plotters of rebellion who, once defeated, were captured; Tachu said to his colleagues: "This comes from misrule in our governance — surely there were errors in between."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the pacification some who had submitted plotted rebellion and were captured; Tachu told his colleagues, "This is the fruit of poor governance on our part — there must have been mistakes along the way."

sentences.zh: 止誅其渠魁，盡釋餘黨。

translations.literal: He executed only the ringleaders and released all the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: He put only the ringleaders to death and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 瑞州張公明愬左丞呂師夔謀為不軌，塔出廉知其誣，曰：「狂夫欲脅求貨耳，若以曚昧言遽聞之朝廷，則大獄茲興，連及無辜。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongming of Ruizhou accused Left Councillor Lü Shiqi of plotting sedition; Tachu investigated and knew it was false, saying: "This madman only wants to extort goods — if vague words are hastily reported to court, a great inquisition will arise and the innocent will be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongming of Ruizhou accused Left Councillor Lü Shiqi of treason; Tachu investigated and found the charge false, saying, "The man is a blackmailer — if we rush vague accusations to court, a great purge will follow and sweep up the innocent.

sentences.zh: 且師夔既居相職，詎肯為狂妄之事！

translations.literal: Moreover Shiqi already holds a councillor's post — how would he undertake reckless deeds!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Shiqi holds a councillor's rank — why would he commit such folly!

sentences.zh: 若遲疑不決，恐彼驚疑，反生異謀。」

translations.literal: If we hesitate and do not decide, I fear they will grow alarmed and in turn hatch strange plots."
translations.idiomatic: If we hesitate, they may panic and turn to fresh conspiracies."

sentences.zh: 乃斬公明而後聞，帝是之。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Gongming and reported afterward; the emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Gongming and reported afterward; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入覲，賜勞有加，復命行省於江西，尋以疾卒於京師，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered audience; additional rewards and consolation were granted; he was again ordered to the Branch Secretariat in Jiangxi; soon he died of illness in the capital at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he came to court and received exceptional honors; he was sent back to head the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat but soon died of illness in the capital, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 妻明理氏，以貞節稱，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Mingli clan, was famed for chaste integrity, and her gate and lane were honored.
translations.idiomatic: His wife of the Mingli clan was celebrated for her fidelity, and the court honored her household.

sentences.zh: 二子：長宰牙，襲爵中奉大夫、江西宣慰使；

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Zaia inherited the rank of Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and became Jiangxi pacification commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder Zaia inherited his father's rank as Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and became pacification commissioner of Jiangxi;

sentences.zh: 次必宰牙，仕至征東行中書省左丞，妻伯牙倫，泰安郡武穆王孛魯歡之女，亦守義有賢行。

translations.literal: the younger Bizaiya rose in office to left councillor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat; his wife Boyalun was the daughter of Prince Wumu Luluhuan of Tai'an Commandery, and she too kept faith and had worthy conduct.
translations.idiomatic: the younger Bizaiya rose to left councillor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat; his wife Boyalun was a daughter of Prince Wumu Luluhuan of Tai'an and was likewise noted for fidelity and virtue.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤

translations.literal: Talichi
translations.idiomatic: Talichi

sentences.zh: 塔里赤，康里人。

translations.literal: Talichi was a man of Kangli.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi was a native of Kangli.

sentences.zh: 其父也里里白，太祖時以武功授帳前緫校，奉旨南徵至洛陽，得唐白樂天故址，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yelilibai, in the Taizu era for military merit was made chief commander before the tent; under imperial order he campaigned south to Luoyang, obtained the old site of the Tang poet Bai Juyi, and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yelilibai, rewarded in the Taizu era for military service with the post of chief commander of the imperial guard, marched south on imperial orders as far as Luoyang, settled on the former estate of the Tang poet Bai Juyi, and made his home there.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤幼穎異，好讀書，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: Talichi in youth was unusually bright, loved reading, and was especially skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi was precocious as a boy, loved books, and excelled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，參佐戎幕，調度軍馬，動合事宜。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post, assisted in the military camp, and in deploying and scheduling troops and horses always matched what the situation required.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post, served on campaign staffs, and in the deployment of men and horses always acted with sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 行省奏充斷事官。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat memorialized that he be made a judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat recommended him as a judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 時南北民戶主客良賤雜糅，蒙古軍牧馬草地互相占據，命塔里赤至其地理之，軍民各得其所，由是世祖知其能。

translations.literal: At that time north and south household registers mixed hosts, guests, free, and servile in confusion; Mongol army horse pastures and grazing lands seized one another's ground; Talichi was ordered to go and survey the terrain; soldiers and civilians each obtained their proper place; thereby the Shizu knew his ability.
translations.idiomatic: North and south household registers were tangled with hosts, tenants, free persons, and bondservants intermixed, while Mongol cavalry pastures and grazing lands encroached on one another; Talichi was sent to survey the terrain and settle boundaries so soldiers and civilians each had their due — the Shizu took note of his ability.

sentences.zh: 俾領蒙古軍圍樊襄，塔里赤躬冒矢石，所向摧陷，樊城破，襄陽降。

translations.literal: He was made to lead Mongol troops in besieging Fan and Xiang; Talichi personally braved arrows and stones; wherever he went he broke and overthrew; Fancheng fell and Xiangyang submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in command of Mongol forces besieging Fan and Xiangyang; Talichi himself stood in the arrow storm and carried every assault; Fancheng fell and Xiangyang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從丞相伯顏渡江，駐臨安，尋命平章奧魯赤等分為六路，追襲宋二王。

translations.literal: He followed Chief Councillor Bayan in crossing the Yangzi, encamped at Lin'an, and soon was ordered with Pacification Commissioner Aoluchi and others to divide into six routes and pursue the two Song princes.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chief Councillor Bayan across the Yangzi and encamped at Lin'an; soon he and Pacification Commissioner Aoluchi and others were divided into six columns to pursue the two Song princes.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤領軍至福建，所過秋毫無犯，降者如歸，宋都統陳宗榮率衆來降。

translations.literal: Talichi led troops to Fujian; wherever he passed not a hair was harmed; those who submitted were as if returning home; the Song commander-in-chief Chen Zongrong led his crowd to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi marched into Fujian without harming a soul along the way; those who submitted came as if to their own homes; the Song commander Chen Zongrong surrendered with his forces.

sentences.zh: 以功遷福建招討使。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Fujian pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡盜起，其最盛者陳吊眼，擁衆五萬，陷漳州。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in many prefectures; the strongest was Chen Diaoyan, who gathered a crowd of fifty thousand and took Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose across the prefectures; the most formidable was Chen Diaoyan, who mustered fifty thousand men and seized Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行省承制命塔里赤為閩廣大都督、征南都元帥，緫四省軍，復漳州，生擒陳吊眼戮于市，餘黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat, acting on its warrant, appointed Talichi Grand Commander of Min-Guang and southern campaign commander-in-chief, commanding the armies of four provinces; he recovered Zhangzhou, captured Chen Diaoyan alive and executed him in the market, and the rest of the faction were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat commissioned Talichi as grand commander of Fujian-Guangdong and southern campaign commander-in-chief over the armies of four provinces; he retook Zhangzhou, captured Chen Diaoyan and executed him in public, and put the remaining rebels to death.

sentences.zh: 繼從征交趾，擊敗黃聖許等，積功加鎮國上將軍、三珠虎符、廣西兩江道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: He then followed the campaign against Jiaozhi, defeated Huang Shengxu and others, and for accumulated merit was advanced to General for the Pacification of the State, the three-pearl tiger tally, and commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Guangxi Two Rivers Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He next campaigned in Jiaozhi, defeated Huang Shengxu and others, and for accumulated merit was promoted to General for the Pacification of the State with the three-pearl tiger tally and made commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Guangxi Two Rivers Circuit.

sentences.zh: 賀州盜起，塔里赤討平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Hezhou; Talichi suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Hezhou, Talichi put them down.

sentences.zh: 改福建宣慰使，又改浙東。

translations.literal: He was changed to Fujian pacification commissioner, and again to Zhe-East.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of Fujian and then of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 金瘡發卒，贈輔國上將軍、浙東道宣慰使都元帥、護軍，追封臨安郡公。

translations.literal: An old wound reopened and he died; he was posthumously made Supporting-State General, commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit, and protector of the army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An old battle wound reopened and he died; he was posthumously made Supporting-State General, commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit, protector of the army, and Duke of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 子二人：脫脫木兒，邵武汀州新軍萬戶府達魯花赤；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Tuotuomuer, darughachi of the Xin Army Ten-thousand Household Office of Shaowu Tingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Tuotuomuer, darughachi of the Xin Army Ten-thousand Household Office at Shaowu-Tingzhou;

sentences.zh: 萬奴，廣西宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: Wannu, commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wannu, commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒

translations.literal: Tahaitiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Tahaitiemuer

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒，荅荅里帶人。

translations.literal: Tahaitiemuer was a man of the Dadalidai people.
translations.idiomatic: Tahaitiemuer was of the Dadalidai people.

sentences.zh: 其先在太祖時事國王木華黎，將左手大萬戶下蒙古軍，鎮太原以西八州。

translations.literal: His ancestor in the Taizu era served King Muqali, commanding the Mongol army under the Left Hand Great Ten-thousand Household, and garrisoned the eight prefectures west of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear had served King Muqali under the Taizu, commanding the Mongol forces of the Left Hand Great Ten-thousand Household and garrisoning the eight prefectures west of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 破金將王公佐軍，斬公佐。

translations.literal: He broke the army of the Jin general Wang Gongzuo and beheaded Gongzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the Jin general Wang Gongzuo and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 從攻陝右，征河西，滅金，皆有功，賜種田戶二百七十。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking the right of Shaanxi, campaigned in Hexi, and in destroying Jin all had merit; he was granted two hundred seventy farming households.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in western Shaanxi and the Hexi campaigns and shared in the destruction of Jin, earning two hundred seventy farming households as reward.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忒木勒哥嗣，從都元帥塔海紺卜征蜀，死於興元。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Temulege succeeded and followed the commander-in-chief Tahai Ganbu in campaigning in Shu, dying at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Temulege succeeded him and followed Commander-in-Chief Tahai Ganbu on the Shu campaign, dying at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖扎剌帶嗣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhaladai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhaladai succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 扎剌帶卒，父拜荅兒尚幼，從祖扎里、荅朮相繼襲其職。

translations.literal: When Zhaladai died, his father Baisaer was still young; his uncles Zhali and Dashu in turn succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaladai died, Baisaer was still a boy, and his uncles Zhali and Dashu held the office in succession.

sentences.zh: 扎里從都元帥大荅征蜀，以所統軍二百人破宋軍于巴州，斬首三百級，生擒五十餘人。

translations.literal: Zhali followed the commander-in-chief Dada in campaigning in Shu; with two hundred troops under his command he broke the Song army at Bazhou, beheaded three hundred, and captured alive more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhali followed Commander-in-Chief Dada on the Shu campaign; with two hundred men he routed the Song at Bazhou, took three hundred heads, and captured more than fifty alive.

sentences.zh: 荅朮以西川行樞密院檄領兵三千人救碉門，大敗宋軍，斬首三百餘級，俘百餘人以歸。

translations.literal: Dashu, on the warrant of the Western Sichuan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, led three thousand troops to relieve Diaomen, utterly defeated the Song army, beheaded more than three hundred, and returned with more than one hundred captives.
translations.idiomatic: On orders from the Western Sichuan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, Dashu led three thousand men to relieve Diaomen, crushed the Song army, took more than three hundred heads, and brought back over a hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 拜荅兒既長，始以父官從行省也速帶兒征建都，死軍中。

translations.literal: When Baisaer had grown up he first held his father's office and followed the Branch Secretariat's Yesudaier in campaigning against Jiandu, dying in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Baisaer came of age he inherited his father's post and followed Yesudaier of the branch secretariat against Jiandu, dying on campaign.

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒襲父職，初從行院忽敦圍嘉定，嘉定降。

translations.literal: Tahaitiemuer inherited his father's post; at first he followed the branch bureau's Hudun in besieging Jiading, and Jiading submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tahaitiemuer succeeded his father; he first served under Hudun of the branch bureau at the siege of Jiading, which then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進圍重慶，守將張珏出師迎敵，塔海帖木兒力戰陷陣，功最多。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Chongqing, the defending general Zhang Jue led troops out to meet the enemy; Tahaitiemuer fought fiercely and broke the line, his merit being greatest.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Chongqing; when the defender Zhang Jue marched out to give battle, Tahaitiemuer fought through the enemy line and won the highest distinction.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又以都魯軍二百人破宋軍於白水江，奪戰船一，俘其衆十三人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, again with two hundred Dulu troops he broke the Song army at the Baishui River, seized one warship, and captured thirteen of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he again routed the Song at the Baishui River with two hundred Dulu troops, captured a warship, and took thirteen prisoners.

sentences.zh: 陞宣武將軍、管軍緫管。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and commander of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and made commander of troops.

sentences.zh: 從也速荅兒征亦奚不薛，又從征都掌蠻，皆以為前鋒，殺獲甚衆。

translations.literal: He followed Yesudaier in campaigning against Yixibuxue, and again in campaigning against the Duzhang Man; in both he served as vanguard and killed and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yesudaier against Yixibuxue and again against the Duzhang tribes, serving as vanguard in both campaigns with heavy kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 九溪蠻、散貓、大盤蠻尚木的世用等叛，從行省曲立吉思帥師往討，皆擒之，及殺其酋長頭狗等。

translations.literal: The Jiuxi Man, Sanmao, the Dapan Man Shangmu, Shiyong, and others rebelled; he followed the Branch Secretariat's Qulijisi in leading troops to punish them, captured them all, and killed their chieftains Tougou and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiuxi tribes, Sanmao, Shangmu of the Dapan Man, Shiyong, and others rebelled, he marched under Qulijisi of the branch secretariat, captured them all, and executed chieftains including Tougou.

sentences.zh: 也速荅兒、藥剌罕率兵萬人會雲南兵討烏蒙蠻，至鬧竈，其酋長阿蒙率五百餘衆奔麻布蠻地，塔海帖木兒以四百人追至山箐中，大敗之，擒阿蒙以歸。

translations.literal: Yesudaier and Yalahan led ten thousand troops to join Yunnan forces in punishing the Wumeng Man; reaching Naozao, their chieftain Ameng led more than five hundred followers to flee into Mabu Man territory; Tahaitiemuer with four hundred pursued into the mountain ravines, utterly defeated them, and captured Ameng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yesudaier and Yalahan led ten thousand men to join Yunnan forces against the Wumeng tribes; at Naozao the chieftain Ameng fled into Mabu territory with five hundred followers; Tahaitiemuer pursued with four hundred into the ravines, routed them, and brought Ameng back captive.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，又從也速荅兒西征，不知所終。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again followed Yesudaier on the western campaign, and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he again followed Yesudaier westward and was never heard from again.

sentences.zh: 口兒吉

translations.literal: Kou'erji
translations.idiomatic: Kou'erji

sentences.zh: 忽都，蒙古兀羅帶氏。

translations.literal: Hudu was of the Mongol Wuluodai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hudu belonged to the Mongol Wuluodai clan.

sentences.zh: 父孛罕，事太祖，備宿衛。

translations.literal: His father Bohuan served the Taizu and was assigned to palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bohuan had served the Taizu as an imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 至太宗時為鎮西行省，領蒙古、漢軍從攻河中、潼關、河南，與拜只思、扎忽歹、阿思蘭攻秦鞏及仁和諸堡，又與拜只思守京兆。

translations.literal: In the Taizong era he was made the Western Pacification Branch Secretariat, leading Mongol and Han troops in following attacks on Hezhong, Tongguan, and Henan; with Baizisi, Zhahudai, and Asilan he attacked the Qin-Gong and Renhe forts; again with Baizisi he defended Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taizong he headed the Western Pacification Branch Secretariat, leading Mongol and Han forces against Hezhong, Tongguan, and Henan; with Baizisi, Zhahudai, and Asilan he stormed the Qin-Gong and Renhe strongholds, and with Baizisi he held Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，授左手萬戶，從都元帥荅海鉗卜出征，卒軍中。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year he was made Left Hand Ten-thousand Household and followed the commander-in-chief Dahai Qianbu on campaign, dying in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei he was made commander of the Left Hand Ten-thousand Household and followed Commander-in-Chief Dahai Qianbu on campaign, dying in the field.

sentences.zh: 子扎忽帶，時在宿衛，弟忽都荅立襲其職。

translations.literal: His son Zhahudai was then in palace guard service; his younger brother Hududali succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhahudai was then on palace guard duty; his younger brother Hududali succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: 忽都荅立卒，札忽帶嗣，為千戶，從行樞密院圍重慶。

translations.literal: When Hududali died, Zhahudai succeeded, became a thousand-household commander, and followed the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs in besieging Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hududali died, Zhahudai succeeded as thousand-household commander and joined the branch bureau's siege of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 重慶守張珏遣勁兵數千出挑戰，札忽帶力戰大破之。

translations.literal: Chongqing's defender Zhang Jue sent several thousand crack troops out to challenge battle; Zhahudai fought fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue, the defender of Chongqing, sent out several thousand elite troops; Zhahudai met them in fierce combat and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 回軍圍瀘州，未下，行樞密院遣入朝計事，授宣武將軍、管軍緫管。

translations.literal: The army turned back to besiege Luzhou, which was not yet taken; the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs sent him to court to plan affairs, and he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and commander of troops.
translations.idiomatic: The army turned to besiege Luzhou, which had not yet fallen; the branch bureau sent him to court to report, and he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and commander of troops.

sentences.zh: 復還攻瀘，登城，與瀘兵搏戰而死。

translations.literal: He returned again to attack Lu, scaled the wall, and died fighting hand to hand with the Luzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the assault on Luzhou, scaled the walls, and died fighting the garrison hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 子阿都赤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Aduchi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Aduchi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孛兒速

translations.literal: Beiersu
translations.idiomatic: Beiersu

sentences.zh: 孛兒速，脫脫忒氏。

translations.literal: Beiersu was of the Tuotuote clan.
translations.idiomatic: Beiersu belonged to the Tuotuote clan.

sentences.zh: 世祖時直宿衛，扈駕征哈剌章還，帝駐蹕高阜，見河北有駕舟而來者，顧謂左右曰：「是賊也，奈何？」

translations.literal: In the Shizu era he was on direct palace guard duty; escorting the imperial carriage on the campaign against Harzhang and returning, the emperor halted on a high mound and saw on the north bank someone coming in a boat; he turned and said to those at his side: "That is a bandit — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shizu he served on direct palace guard; returning from the Harzhang campaign, the emperor halted on a height and saw someone rowing across from the north bank; he turned to his attendants and said, "That is an enemy — what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 孛兒速進曰：「臣請禦之。」

translations.literal: Beiersu advanced and said: "Your servant asks to meet him."
translations.idiomatic: Beiersu stepped forward and said, "Let your servant deal with him."

sentences.zh: 即解衣徑渡，揮戈刺死舟尾二人，拏其舟就岸，舟中之人倉惶失措，帝命左右悉擒之。

translations.literal: He at once stripped off his clothes, crossed straight over, waved his spear and stabbed to death the two men at the boat's stern, drew the boat to shore, and the men in the boat were flustered and at a loss; the emperor ordered those at his side to seize them all.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped, swam across, killed the two men at the stern with his spear, pulled the boat to shore, and when those aboard panicked the emperor ordered his attendants to seize them all.

sentences.zh: 哈剌章平，以功論賞。

translations.literal: When Harzhang was pacified, rewards were apportioned according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Harzhang was pacified, he received his share of the rewards for merit.

sentences.zh: 子荅荅呵兒，從征孛可有功，由宿衛陞武德將軍、揭只揭烈溫千戶所達魯花赤。

translations.literal: His son Dadaheer followed the campaign against Boke with merit; from palace guard he was raised to General of Martial Virtue and darughachi of the Jiezhijieliewen Ten-thousand Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dadaheer distinguished himself in the campaign against Boke and rose from the palace guard to General of Martial Virtue and darughachi of the Jiezhijieliewen Ten-thousand Household Office.

sentences.zh: 從征叛王乃顏、也不干等，奮戈擊死數人，擒也不干，收其所管欽察之民。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the rebel princes Nayan, Yebogan, and others; wielding his spear he struck and killed several men, captured Yebogan, and received the Qincha people under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the rebel princes Nayan and Yebogan, killed several men in combat, captured Yebogan, and took charge of the Qincha people under his command.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，進懷遠大將軍、元帥，卒。

translations.literal: In the Wuzong era he was advanced to General of Cherished Distance and marshal, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wuzong he was promoted to General of Cherished Distance and marshal, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 月舉連赤海牙

translations.literal: Yuejulianchihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Yuejulianchihaiya

sentences.zh: 月舉連赤海牙，畏兀兒人。

translations.literal: Yuejulianchihaiya was a man of the Uyghur people.
translations.idiomatic: Yuejulianchihaiya was a Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 從憲宗征釣魚山，奉命修麴藥以療師疫，賞白金五十兩。

translations.literal: He followed the Xianzong in campaigning at Diaoyushan, received orders to prepare medicinal yeast to treat the army's pestilence, and was rewarded with fifty taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Xianzong at Diaoyushan, was ordered to brew medicinal yeast to treat the army's epidemic, and was rewarded with fifty taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 繼從太子滿哥都征雲南，戰數勝。

translations.literal: He then followed the crown prince Mangudu in campaigning in Yunnan and won several battles.
translations.idiomatic: He next followed Crown Prince Mangudu into Yunnan and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，火都暨荅離叛，領兵與討平之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Huodu and Dali rebelled; he led troops to join in suppressing and pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong, when Huodu and Dali rebelled, he led troops that helped put them down.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，佩虎符，為隴右河西道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he bore the tiger tally and became surveillance commissioner for criminal matters of the Longyou Hexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12 he received the tiger tally and was made surveillance commissioner for the Longyou-Hexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 兀朗孫火石顏謀亂，從皇太子安西王往鎮之，皇太子賜以白金五十兩。

translations.literal: Wulangsun Huoshiyan plotted rebellion; he followed the crown prince, the Anxi Prince, to pacify the region, and the crown prince bestowed fifty taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulangsun Huoshiyan plotted rebellion, he followed Crown Prince Anxi to pacify the region and received fifty taels of white gold from the prince.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與伯速帶平土魯，皇子復賜金衣腰帶金碗，且以其功聞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, with Bosudai he pacified Tulu; the prince again bestowed a golden robe, belt, and golden bowl, and reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he and Bosudai pacified Tulu; the prince again gave him a golden robe, belt, and bowl, and reported his achievements to court.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進官嘉議大夫，仍居舊職。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced in office to Grand Master of Palace Counsellor and still held his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Counsellor while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進中奉大夫、四川等處行中書省參知政事，尋以疾歸秦州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was advanced to Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and vice administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat; soon he returned to Qinzhou on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made Grand Master for the Promotion of Governance and vice administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, but soon retired to Qinzhou because of illness.

sentences.zh: 大德八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 至順中，贈推忠宣力定遠功臣、資善大夫、陝西行省左丞、護軍，追封威寧郡公，諡襄靖。

translations.literal: In the Zhishun era he was posthumously made Meritorious Minister for Loyal Promotion and Pacification at a Distance, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, left councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and protector of the army; enfeoffed as Duke of Weining Commandery and given the posthumous title Xiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhishun era he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister for Loyal Promotion and Pacification at a Distance, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, left councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and protector of the army, enfeoffed as Duke of Weining with the posthumous name Xiangjing.

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤

translations.literal: Adachi
translations.idiomatic: Adachi

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Adachi was of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Adachi was an Alan.

sentences.zh: 父昂和思，憲宗時佩虎符為萬戶。

translations.literal: His father Anghesi, in the Xianzong era bore the tiger tally as ten-thousand household commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anghesi had held the tiger tally as ten-thousand household commander under the Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤扈從憲宗南征，與敵兵戰于劍州，以功賞白銀。

translations.literal: Adachi escorted the Xianzong on the southern campaign, fought the enemy at Jianzhou, and for merit was rewarded with white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Adachi accompanied the Xianzong on the southern campaign, fought at Jianzhou, and was rewarded with silver for his service.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥叛，從也兒怯等征之，有功。

translations.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he followed Yierqie and others in campaigning against him and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he campaigned under Yierqie and others and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統三年，從征李璮，身二十餘戰，累功授金符千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong of the Shizu he followed the campaign against Li Tan, personally fought in more than twenty battles, and for accumulated merit was made golden-tally thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 3 of the Shizu reign he fought against Li Tan in more than twenty engagements and, for accumulated merit, was made a golden-tally thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏、平章阿朮之平江南也，阿荅赤皆在行中，著戰功，歿于陣，帝憐之，特賜鈔七十錠、白金五百兩，為葬具，仍賜鎮巢之民一千五百三十九戶，命其子伯荅兒襲職。

translations.literal: When Chief Councillor Bayan and Pacification Commissioner Azhu pacified Jiangnan, Adachi was in the army throughout, showed battle merit, and died in the line; the emperor pitied him and specially granted seventy ingots of paper money and five hundred taels of white gold for funeral goods, and still granted one thousand five hundred thirty-nine households of Zhenchao, ordering his son Bodai'er to succeed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Bayan and Pacification Commissioner Azhu conquered the south, Adachi was with the army throughout, distinguished himself in battle, and fell in the field; the emperor took pity on him, granted seventy ingots of paper money and five hundred taels of white gold for his burial, assigned him 1,539 households at Zhenchao, and ordered his son Bodai'er to succeed to his post.

sentences.zh: 伯荅兒從別急列迷失北征，與瓮吉剌只兒瓦台戰于牙里伴朶之地，以功受上賞。

translations.literal: Bodai'er followed Bieji Liemishi on the northern campaign and fought Wengjilazhi'ertai at Yalibanduo; for merit he received the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: Bodai'er followed Bieji Liemishi on the northern campaign and fought Wengjilazhi'ertai at Yalibanduo, earning the highest reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 尋進定遠大將軍、後衛都指揮使，兼右阿速衛事，將阿速軍往征別失八里，與敵兵累戰累捷。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General for Pacification at a Distance and commander of the Rear Guard, and concurrently charged with the Right Alan Guard; leading Alan troops he campaigned toward Bieshibali and with the enemy fought repeatedly with repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General for Pacification at a Distance and commander of the Rear Guard, with charge of the Right Alan Guard; leading Alan troops against Bieshibali he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 樞密臣以其功聞，賞白金、貂裘、弓矢、鞍轡等，尋復以銀坐椅賜之。

translations.literal: A Bureau of Military Affairs official reported his merit; he was rewarded with white gold, sable fur coats, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, and the like; soon he was again granted a silver chair.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported his achievements; he received white gold, sable coats, bows, arrows, saddles, and bridles, and soon afterward a silver chair as well.

sentences.zh: 明安，康里氏。

translations.literal: Ming'an was of the Kangli clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an was a Kangli.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，世祖詔民之蕩析離居及僧道、漏籍諸色人不當差徭者萬餘人充貴赤，令明安領之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan the Shizu decreed that more than ten thousand people among the populace scattered and separated from their homes, monks and Daoists, persons omitted from registers, and persons of various categories not liable for corvée should fill the Kuechi ranks, and ordered Ming'an to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 the Shizu decreed that more than ten thousand displaced persons, monks, Daoists, unregistered persons, and others not liable for corvée should be enrolled in the Kuechi guard, with Ming'an placed in command.

sentences.zh: 明安歲扈駕出入，克勤于事。

translations.literal: Ming'an each year escorted the imperial carriage in and out and was diligent in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Ming'an attended the emperor on his journeys and served with tireless diligence.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授定遠大將軍、中衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed General for Pacification at a Distance and commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made General for Pacification at a Distance and commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜佩虎符，領貴赤軍北征。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted the tiger tally and led Kuechi troops on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the tiger tally and led the Kuechi guard north.

sentences.zh: 又明年，立貴赤親軍都指揮使司，命為本衛達魯花赤。

translations.literal: The year after that the Kuechi Imperial Guard Command was established, and he was ordered to be darughachi of that guard.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that the Kuechi Imperial Guard Command was established and he was made its darughachi.

sentences.zh: 尋奉旨領蒙古軍八千北征，明年，至別失八剌哈思之地，與海都軍戰有功。

translations.literal: Soon he received orders to lead eight thousand Mongol troops on the northern campaign; the next year, reaching the land of Bieshibalahasi, he fought the army of Kaidu with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered north with eight thousand Mongol troops; the next year, reaching Bieshibalahasi, he fought Kaidu's army with distinction.

sentences.zh: 二十六年冬十二月，別乞憐叛，劫取官站脫脫火孫塔剌海等，明安率衆追擊之，五戰五捷，悉還之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of the twenty-sixth year, Bieqiling rebelled and plundered the official relay stations of Tuotuohuosuntalahai and others; Ming'an led the crowd in pursuit, fought five battles with five victories, and recovered them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-sixth year, when Bieqiling rebelled and raided relay stations including Tuotuohuosuntalahai, Ming'an pursued him, won five battles in succession, and recovered everything taken.

sentences.zh: 至杭海，強民闊闊台、撒兒塔台等率衆作亂，奪三站地，劫脫脫火孫，明安引兵又追擊之，却其軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Hanghai, powerful men Kuokuotai, Saertatai, and others led crowds in revolt, seized the lands of three stations, and plundered Tuotuohuosun; Ming'an led troops again in pursuit and drove back their army.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanghai the strongmen Kuokuotai and Saertatai rose in revolt, seized three relay stations, and plundered Tuotuohuosun; Ming'an pursued again and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二十七年秋七月，布四麻、當先別乞失、出春伯駙馬、兀者台、朶羅台、兀兒荅兒、塔里雅赤等掠四怯薛牛馬畜牧，及劫滅烈太子昔博赤并斡脫、布伯各投下民殆盡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of the twenty-seventh year, Busima, Dangxianbieqishi, the consort prince Chuchunbo, Wuzhatai, Duoluotai, Wuerda'er, Taliyachi, and others plundered the cattle, horses, and herds of the four keshig, and plundered nearly all the people under the princely establishments of Prince Mielie Xibochi and Wotuo and Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year, Busima, Dangxianbieqishi, Consort Prince Chuchunbo, Wuzhatai, Duoluotai, Wuerda'er, Taliyachi, and others raided livestock of the four keshig guards and plundered nearly all the households under the establishments of Prince Mielie Xibochi, Wotuo, and Bobo.

sentences.zh: 明安將兵追擊于汪吉昔博赤之城，賊軍敗走，還所掠之民并獲其牛馬畜牧等以歸。

translations.literal: Ming'an led troops in pursuit at the city of Wangjixibochi; the rebel army was defeated and fled; he returned the plundered people and also captured their cattle, horses, herds, and the like and came back.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an pursued them to Wangjixibochi, routed the rebels, restored the people they had taken, and brought back their livestock.

sentences.zh: 時出伯、伯都所領軍乏食，奉旨以明安所獲畜牧濟之。

translations.literal: At that time the armies led by Chubor and Bodu lacked food; on imperial order the herds Ming'an had captured were used to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Chubor and Bodu were then short of provisions; by imperial order Ming'an's captured herds were used to feed them.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以功陞定遠大將軍、貴赤親軍都指揮使司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, for merit he was raised to General for Pacification at a Distance and darughachi of the Kuechi Imperial Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to General for Pacification at a Distance and darughachi of the Kuechi Imperial Guard Command for his service.

sentences.zh: 時別失八剌哈孫盜起，詔以兵討之，戰于別失八里禿兒古闍，有功，賊軍再合四千人於忽蘭兀孫，明安設方略與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Bieshibalahasi; he was ordered to campaign against them with troops; he fought at Bieshibali Tuerhujian with merit; the bandit army gathered again four thousand men at Hulanwusun; Ming'an laid plans and fought, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Bieshibalahasi he was ordered to suppress them, fought with distinction at Bieshibali Tuerhujian, and when four thousand rebels regrouped at Hulanwusun he devised a plan and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，復將兵北征，與海都戰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he again led troops on the northern campaign and fought Kaidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade he again led troops north and fought Kaidu.

sentences.zh: 七年，歿于軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 子曰帖哥台，曰孛蘭奚。

translations.literal: His sons were Tiegetai and Bolanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Tiegetai and Bolanxi.

sentences.zh: 孛蘭奚，昭武大將軍、中衛親軍都指揮使，積官銀青榮祿大夫、太尉。

translations.literal: Bolanxi was General of Martial Brilliance and commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army, and through accumulated offices reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Pendants and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Bolanxi rose to General of Martial Brilliance and commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army, and through successive promotions reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Pendants and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子桑兀孫，中衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Sangwusun was commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sangwusun became commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army.

sentences.zh: 桑兀孫卒，弟乞荅海襲職。

translations.literal: When Sangwusun died, his younger brother Qidahai succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangwusun died, his younger brother Qidahai succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: 忽林失

translations.literal: Hulinshi
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi

sentences.zh: 忽林失，八魯剌氏。

translations.literal: Hulinshi was of the Baluosi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi belonged to the Baluosi clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖不魯罕罕劄，事太祖，從平諸國，充八魯剌思千戶，以其軍與太赤溫等戰，重傷墜馬，帝親勒兵救之，以功陞萬戶，賜黃金五十兩、白金五百兩，俾直宿衛。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Buluhanhanzha served the Taizu, followed in pacifying the various states, served as thousand-household commander of the Baluosi, and with his army fought Taichiwen and others; severely wounded he fell from his horse; the emperor personally led troops to rescue him; for merit he was raised to ten-thousand household commander, granted fifty taels of yellow gold and five hundred taels of white gold, and made to serve on direct palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Buluhanhanzha served the Taizu in the conquest of the realm, commanded a Baluosi thousand-household, and in battle against Taichiwen was gravely wounded and thrown from his horse; the Taizu personally led troops to his rescue, promoted him to ten-thousand household commander, granted him fifty taels of gold and five hundred of silver, and assigned him to direct palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 祖許兒台，年十五能馳射賊，以勇略稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuertai at age fifteen could ride and shoot at bandits and was famed for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuertai could ride and shoot down bandits at fifteen and was famed for courage and resource.

sentences.zh: 從定宗征欽察，為千戶。

translations.literal: He followed the Dingzong in campaigning against the Qincha and became a thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Dingzong against the Qincha and became a thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 領兵下西番。

translations.literal: He led troops down into the Western Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops into the western borderlands.

sentences.zh: 從世祖伐宋，至亳州，與宋人迎敵，敗之。

translations.literal: He followed the Shizu in attacking Song; reaching Bozhou he met the Song in battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Shizu against the Song; at Bozhou he met the enemy and routed them.

sentences.zh: 父瓮吉剌帶，初為軍器監官，從世祖親征阿里不哥，以功受上賞。

translations.literal: His father Wengjiladai was at first an official of the Armory Directorate; he followed the Shizu in personally campaigning against Ariq Böke and for merit received the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wengjiladai first served in the Armory Directorate; he accompanied the Shizu's personal campaign against Ariq Böke and received the highest reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 俄奉旨使西域，籍地產，悉得其實。

translations.literal: Soon he received orders as envoy to the Western Regions to register land and produce, and obtained the facts in full.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to the Western Regions to register land and produce and reported with complete accuracy.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲大用之而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor was just about to employ him on a grand scale when he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on the point of giving him high office when he died.

sentences.zh: 忽林失初直宿衛。

translations.literal: Hulinshi at first served on direct palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi began as a direct palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 後以千戶從征乃顏，馳馬奮戈，衝擊敵營，矢下如雨，身被三十三創。

translations.literal: Later as thousand-household commander he followed the campaign against Nayan; spurring his horse and brandishing his spear he charged the enemy camp; arrows fell like rain; his body took thirty-three wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as thousand-household commander on the campaign against Nayan, he spurred his horse, leveled his spear, and charged the enemy camp through a rain of arrows, taking thirty-three wounds.

sentences.zh: 成宗親督左右出其鏃，命醫療之，以其功聞。

translations.literal: The Chengzong personally supervised those at his side in drawing out the arrowheads, ordered him medically treated, and reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzong personally supervised the extraction of the arrowheads, ordered him treated, and reported his deeds to court.

sentences.zh: 世祖以克宋所得銀甕及金酒器等賜之，命領太府監。

translations.literal: The Shizu granted him the silver urns and gold wine vessels and the like taken in conquering Song and ordered him to head the Imperial Storehouse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu rewarded him with silver urns and gold wine vessels from the Song conquest and appointed him head of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 後以千戶從皇子闊闊出出征，還，留鎮軍中。

translations.literal: Later as thousand-household commander he followed Prince Kuokuochu on campaign; on returning he was left to garrison the army.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Prince Kuokuochu on campaign as thousand-household commander and, on returning, was left to garrison the army.

sentences.zh: 後從成宗與海都、都瓦等戰有功，成宗嘉之，特命為翰林承旨，俄改萬戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Chengzong in fighting Kaidu, Duwa, and others with merit; the Chengzong praised him and specially appointed him Hanlin executive academician; soon he was changed to ten-thousand household commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought under the Chengzong against Kaidu and Duwa with distinction; the Chengzong praised him, made him Hanlin executive academician, and soon restored him to ten-thousand household command.

sentences.zh: 與叛王斡羅思、察八兒等戰，以功授榮祿大夫、司徒，賜銀印。

translations.literal: He fought the rebel princes Woluosi, Chaba'er, and others; for merit he was made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and Minister of Education and granted a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebel princes Woluosi and Chaba'er and, for his service, was made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan and Minister of Education with a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 武宗嘗曰：「群臣中能為國宣力如忽林失者實鮮，其厚賚之。」

translations.literal: The Wuzong once said: "Among the ministers, those who can exert strength for the state like Hulinshi are truly few — reward him generously."
translations.idiomatic: The Wuzong once said, "Few among my ministers serve the state with the force Hulinshi does — reward him generously."

sentences.zh: 於是遣使召見。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to summon him to audience.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 未幾武宗崩，仁宗即位，念其舊勳，賞賚特厚。

translations.literal: Before long the Wuzong died; the Renzong succeeded; remembering his old merit, he granted rewards especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Wuzong died and the Renzong succeeded; remembering his long service, the new emperor rewarded him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒

translations.literal: Shilabadou'er
translations.idiomatic: Shilabadou'er

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Shilabadou'er was of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilabadou'er was an Alan.

sentences.zh: 父月魯達某，憲宗時領阿速十人入覲，充阿塔赤，從世祖至哈剌章之地，戰數勝，兀里羊哈台以其功聞，賜所俘人一口以賞之，後以金瘡發卒。

translations.literal: His father Yueludamou, in the Xianzong era led ten Alan men to audience, served as atachi, followed the Shizu to the land of Harzhang, won several battles; Wuliyanghatai reported his merit; he was granted one captive person as reward; later an old wound reopened and he died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yueludamou had led ten Alan warriors to audience under the Xianzong, served as an atachi, followed the Shizu to Harzhang, and won repeated victories; Wuliyanghatai reported his merit and he was rewarded with a captive; an old wound later reopened and he died.

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒至自脫別之地，帝特賜白金、楮幣、牛馬等物。

translations.literal: When Shilabadou'er arrived from the land of Tuobie, the emperor specially bestowed white gold, paper currency, cattle and horses, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilabadou'er returned from Tuobie, the emperor specially granted him white gold, paper money, cattle, horses, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，從丞相伯顏南征有功，仍充阿塔赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan he followed Chief Councillor Bayan on the southern campaign with merit and again served as atachi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 21 he distinguished himself on Chief Councillor Bayan's southern campaign and again served as an atachi.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命放海青，曰：「能獲新者賞之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered sea hawks released, saying: "Whoever can obtain a fresh catch shall be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered his sea hawks flown and said, "Whoever brings back a fresh kill shall be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒即援弓射一兔二禽以獻，賞沙魚皮雜帶及貂裘，且命於尚乘寺為少卿、於阿速為千戶。

translations.literal: Shilabadou'er at once took his bow and shot one rabbit and two birds to present; he was rewarded with a shark-skin mixed belt and a sable fur coat, and was ordered to be vice director of the Imperial Transport Directorate and thousand-household commander among the Alan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilabadou'er immediately took his bow, brought down a rabbit and two birds, and presented them; he was rewarded with a shark-skin belt and a sable coat and appointed vice director of the Imperial Transport Directorate and Alan thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授武略將軍，管阿速軍千戶，賜金符。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General of Martial Strategy, commanded the Alan army thousand-household, and was granted the golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was made General of Martial Strategy, placed in command of an Alan thousand-household, and granted the golden tally.

sentences.zh: 乃顏叛，從諸王和元魯往征之，力戰有功。

translations.literal: When Nayan rebelled, he followed Prince Heyuanlu to campaign against him and fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan rebelled, he marched under Prince Heyuanlu and distinguished himself in fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 乃顏平，帝賞以金腰帶及銀交床等。

translations.literal: When Nayan was pacified, the emperor rewarded him with a golden belt and a silver folding couch and the like.
translations.idiomatic: After Nayan's defeat the emperor rewarded him with a golden belt, a silver folding couch, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，進武德將軍、尚乘寺少卿，兼阿速千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was advanced to General of Martial Virtue and vice director of the Imperial Transport Directorate, concurrently Alan thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to General of Martial Virtue and vice director of the Imperial Transport Directorate, while retaining his Alan thousand-household command.

sentences.zh: 征哈荅安等，敗之，獲其駝馬等物。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Hada'an and others, he defeated them and seized their camels, horses, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Hada'an and others he routed them and captured their camels, horses, and other booty.

sentences.zh: 成宗嘉其功，以軍二千益之。

translations.literal: The Chengzong praised his merit and increased his army by two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzong praised his achievements and added two thousand troops to his command.

sentences.zh: 討叛王脫脫，擒之，以功受賞。

translations.literal: Punishing the rebel prince Tuotuo, he captured him and received reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the rebel prince Tuotuo, captured him, and was rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 大德六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 子那海產，襲其職。

translations.literal: His son Nahaiyan succeeded to his post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nahaiyan succeeded to his office.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，進宣武將軍、右衛阿速親軍都指揮使，賜三珠虎符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was advanced to General of Manifest Martiality and commander of the Right Guard Alan Imperial Army, and granted the three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 2 he was promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and commander of the Right Guard Alan Imperial Army, with the three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，覃加明威將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was broadly advanced to General of Manifest Might.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 2 he was further promoted to General of Manifest Might.

sentences.zh: 徹里，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Cheli was of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli was an Alan.

sentences.zh: 父別吉八，在憲宗時從攻釣魚山，以功受賞。

translations.literal: His father Biejiba, in the Xianzong era followed the attack on Diaoyushan and received reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biejiba had followed the Xianzong at Diaoyushan and been rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 徹里事世祖，充火兒赤。

translations.literal: Cheli served the Shizu and filled the post of kuo'erchi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli served the Shizu as a kuo'erchi attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征海都，奮戈擊其前鋒，官軍二人陷陣，掖而出之，以功受賞。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Kaidu, he brandished his spear and struck their vanguard; two government troops fell into the line; he supported them and brought them out; for merit he received reward.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Kaidu he charged the enemy vanguard, rescued two soldiers trapped in the line, and was rewarded for his bravery.

sentences.zh: 後從征杭海，獲其牛馬畜牧，悉以給軍食。

translations.literal: Later following the campaign at Hanghai, he seized their cattle, horses, and herds and used them all to supply the army's food.
translations.idiomatic: On a later campaign at Hanghai he captured enemy livestock and used it all to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賞鈔三千五百錠，仍以分賚士卒。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and rewarded three thousand five hundred ingots of paper money, and still distributed shares to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, granted 3,500 ingots of paper money, and shared the reward among his men.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，盜據博落脫兒之地，命將兵討之，獲三千餘人，誅其酋長還。
